Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the sideswipe incident you
reported in Sugar Land, Texas. Can you satte your full name for the record?
A: I'd rather keep my name off this one, if that's all right. Just call me the driver.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened?
A: I was on a multi-lane road in Sugar Land, heading toward the highway. I was changing lanes to get over for my
exit.
Q: Did you check your mirrors and signal before you moved over?
A: I checked the mirror and I signaled. I didn't see the other car in my blind spot until it was too late.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other vehicle sideswiped the rear passenger side of my car. We both pulled to the shoulder. The other driver
said he was sorry and then we exchanged information.
Q: Did you or anyone else require medical attention at the scene?
A: No ambulance. I felt fine at first, but my neck started getting stiff within a few hours. By the next morning I had pain
running into my shoulders and headaches.
Q: Have you sought treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to a clinic and they diagnosed whiplash. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week and I take
muscle relaxers at night.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. Turning my head to the left is hard, and sitting at my desk for long periods makes it worse. I'm still working,
but I've had to adjust my schedule some days.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Just that I'm cooperating fully and I want this handled fairly. I have the clinic paperwork and I can send it over.
Q: Thnak you. We'll follow up once we receive those records. This concludes the statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
